title: layout_config plan-gate drift is real but inert: saved ai_* blocks never render (claimed sink is dead code)
description: Verified the backend half of the claim: ai_only/premium layout blocks are stripped only at write time (clean_layout_config via validate_layout_config/_draft and the ai-design apply path), publish_design_draft and customization_restore copy layout_config verbatim, and StoreCustomizationPublicSerializer.to_representation re-filters site_theme/videos/live_stream/accent/review toggles/site_templates but serves layout_config unfiltered. However the claimed impact — ai_* blocks keep rendering after a plan downgrade — is refuted on current source. The only code that mounts saved non-canonical layout_config blocks is BlockRenderer.vue's 'extras' logic, and nothing in the repo imports BlockRenderer.vue (zero references outside its own file and comments). Every live public landing view (all 8 views/store/*/InicioView.vue) resolves blocks through templateBlocks(), which iterates ONLY the template's canonical blocks.<surface> list and overlays saved enabled/variant/props onto canonical ids — non-canonical ids are dropped. No template's canonical blocks.landing contains any ai_* id (verified raiz, mercado, gimnasio, movimiento, sastreria, moderntec, indumentaria, impacto), so saved ai_* blocks are unreachable on every plan. The persisted ai_* entries in the public payload are inert data; there is no rendered entitlement leak.
claimed_root_cause: Plan enforcement for layout blocks exists only in the write-path sanitizer (clean_layout_config); the public serializer trusts stored layout_config and the frontend renderer trusts the payload, with no benefit check on the read/render path.

trace.description: Write-time gate: clean_layout_config(value, has_advanced, has_ai) drops premium blocks without has_design_advanced and ai_only blocks without has_ai_design — but only when the config is PATCHed (draft or published).

customization_publish copies layout_config_draft -> layout_config verbatim (line 53) and site_theme_draft -> site_theme (54); only template_draft is re-checked against allowed_templates_of (58). No re-clean of layout_config at publish.

Restore copies the StudioVersion snapshot's layout_config into both published and draft fields verbatim (1671-1672); template is re-checked against allowed_templates_of at 1683, layout_config is not re-cleaned.

Public read re-filters site_theme via filter_site_theme (724-729), videos cap (714-717), live_stream_url (718-719), accent fields (707-709), review toggles (702-704) and site_templates/show_catalog (733-736) — layout_config is absent from the filtering and served verbatim via super().to_representation.

CLAIMED sink: inserts saved layout_config blocks not in the canonical layout whenever props.components[raw.id] exists (42-53) and mounts them at :119 — REFUTED: this component has zero importers anywhere in frontend/src (repo-wide grep finds only its own file and comments), so this code never executes.

ACTUAL live render path used by every InicioView: iterates only templateDef(id).blocks[surface] canonical entries and overlays saved enabled/variant/props onto matching canonical ids (126-135). Non-canonical ids — including all ai_* ids — are dropped; its own comment states 'un id que el diseño no trae no se agrega aca'.

evidence.description: Reads ctx.custom.layout_config[surface].blocks and mounts saved ids via props.components[raw.id] — but the file is imported by nothing (grep for 'BlockRenderer' repo-wide returns only this file, a comment in blocks/index.js:3, and a CSS comment).
templateBlocks() maps over canonical only; saved blocks only override canonical entries. resolveLayout() (:144) delegates to it.

blocks.landing canonical list contains no ai_* ids; identical check across all 8 template index.js files (gimnasio, impacto, indumentaria, mercado, moderntec, movimiento, sastreria) — none declare aiquote/aistrip/aicheck/aigrid/aiband/aipricing/aiprocess/aimosaic.
landingExtras registers all eight BlkAi* components and views spread them into MAP — but MAP[b.id] is only reached for ids templateBlocks emits, so the registrations are unreachable for ai_* ids.
Representative live path: visible = templateBlocks(pageTemplate,'landing',custom.layout_config).filter(b => b.enabled && MAP[b.id]) — canonical ids only.
Confirms the drift half is real: to_representation filters site_theme/videos/live_stream/accent/reviews/site_templates but never touches layout_config.
Backend tests assert ai_* ids DO land in published layout_config — persisted but, per the frontend analysis, never mounted publicly.

reason: The claimed sink is refuted by current source. BlockRenderer.vue — the sole component implementing 'mount saved non-canonical blocks' — is dead code with zero importers. The live renderer templateBlocks() drops every id not declared in the template's canonical blocks.<surface> list, and no template declares any ai_* id, so saved ai_* blocks cannot mount on the public site on ANY plan (entitled or not). The unfiltered layout_config in the public payload is therefore inert data, not an entitlement leak. The write-time-only gate plus verbatim publish/restore is genuine backend drift worth hardening (re-run clean_layout_config at publish/restore and add a read-side filter, mirroring filter_site_theme), but it produces no rendered paid-tier content after downgrade, so the candidate as stated (paid-tier AI blocks persist AND render) does not hold.

title: No quota on categories, brands or discounts lets a store owner amplify public catalog request cost without bound
description: Category, Brand and Discount creation are gated only by plan flags — catalog_enabled (has_public_link, present on the cheapest paid plan) and has_discounts (premium/ecommerce) — with no count limit anywhere in the viewsets, serializers, models or benefit catalog. Every other owner-writable collection that feeds shared payloads IS capped (max_products rechecked under select_for_update, SERVICES_MAX=24 under lock, image caps). These unbounded collections feed the anonymous public catalog endpoint: running_discount_stamp(store) is evaluated on EVERY request — including cache hits — to build the cache key (one query plus a Python sorted() loop calling campaign.is_running() per in-window discount). On cache miss, _public_catalog_data runs effective_pricing_of per product x per running discount (O(PxD) via winning_discount_of->discount_covers), serializes ALL categories and brands including empty ones, and serializes all running discounts as promotions. Distinct query strings mint distinct cache keys (_params_fingerprint), so varied anonymous filters multiply the miss-path cost. Discount creation additionally fires _broadcast_offer -> notify_store_discount to all store members per create.
root_cause: Resource quotas were applied to products, services and images but never to catalog taxonomy (categories, brands) or discounts, even though all of them are serialized into the shared public catalog payload on every cache miss and discounts are scanned on every request via the cache-key stamp.
intended_behavior: Owner-writable collections that feed shared public payloads should be bounded — per-plan benefit limits or fixed ceilings enforced under select_for_update, the same pattern used for max_products, SERVICES_MAX and the image caps; and the public payload should exclude empty taxonomy rows and cap serialized lists.

trace.description: Owner POST /api/categories/ (BrandViewSet identical at :93): CatalogGateMixin gates create/update/destroy only on catalog_enabled = has_public_link; inherited CatalogBaseViewSet.create does serializer validation + save with no count check.
Owner POST /api/discounts/: gated only by has_discounts flag (:134-143); create (:148-154) has no count check and triggers _broadcast_offer (:166-178) notifying all store members per create.

Generic create path: serializer.is_valid(raise_exception=True) then save(store=my_store()) — no quota hook exists for taxonomy/discount viewsets (contrast: ProductViewSet.create overrides with a locked can_add_product check).

Only per-(store,name) uniqueness is validated; DiscountMixinValidator.validate (:116-178) checks scope ownership/window/products cap (500) but no collection count. Serializers and models add no bound (Category/Brand UniqueConstraint(store,name) at models.py:32,55; Discount has no name constraint at all, models.py:243-245).
Every anonymous GET /api/stores/public/<slug>/catalog/ builds cache_key including running_discount_stamp(store) BEFORE cache_get — the O(active-discounts) stamp cost is paid on hits and misses alike.

Runs a Discount query over all active in-window rows plus a Python sorted() loop calling campaign.is_running(moment) per row — O(D) per public request even on cache hits (:82-90); running_discounts_of (:40-66) repeats the same scan with prefetch on misses.

On cache miss: effective_pricing_of(product, discounts) runs for EVERY active product and winning_discount_of iterates all running discounts per product -> O(PxD) (services.py:127-133); ALL categories/brands serialized unfiltered (:1199-1200, :1238-1239) and all running discounts serialized as promotions (:1236, :1240).

evidence.description: Contrast: ProductViewSet.create rechecks can_add_product under select_for_update inside transaction.atomic (:465-472) — the intended quota pattern taxonomy/discounts lack.
Contrast: ServiceViewSet.create enforces can_add_service/SERVICES_MAX=24 under select_for_update (:48-54).

has_public_link=True on 'Plan basico' (cheapest plan) — sufficient to create unbounded categories/brands; has_discounts only on premium (:162) and ecommerce (:218); dict_benefits (:12-42) defines no max_categories/max_brands/max_discounts benefit.
Discount Meta constraints contain only a percent CheckConstraint — no (store,name) uniqueness and no count bound; Category/Brand uniqueness is per-(store,name) so distinct names are unbounded.
PUBLIC_CACHE_TTL=120 bounds miss-path amortization; PublicReadThrottle on the action (:1005) and 'user':'1000/day' create throttle (settings.py:79-85) bound but do not eliminate the amplification.
_broadcast_offer -> notify_store_discount to all store members on every discount create (:148-154) — mass creation additionally spams the owner's own customers.

conditions.description: Authenticated store owner (IsAuthenticated) with an active subscription: has_public_link suffices for categories/brands (all paid plans); has_discounts requires premium or ecommerce.

Store must be published and publicly reachable: is_published, !is_blocked, has_public_link, show_catalog != False and 'catalog' in effective site_templates, with anonymous traffic (or attacker-generated requests) hitting the public catalog.

Plan benefits seeded per dict_plan_benefits; 'user' throttle = 1000/day caps create throughput, 'public_read' = 1000/hour/IP caps read amplification; Redis cache TTL 120s amortizes the miss path (throttles fail-open if Redis is down, worsening amplification).

execution.attacker_perspective: A paying store owner (cheapest plan suffices for categories/brands; premium/ecommerce for discounts) seeking to inflate the per-request CPU/DB cost and payload size of their store's anonymous public catalog endpoint, degrading shared worker/cache capacity and their own visitors' experience.
payloads: POST /api/categories/ {"name": "cat-<n>"} repeated N times (unique names pass the per-store uniqueness check)
POST /api/discounts/ {"name": "d-<n>", "percent": 10, "scope": "all", "starts_at": "<now>", "is_active": true} repeated N times (ends_at null keeps every row 'running')
GET /api/stores/public/<slug>/catalog/ anonymously, repeated with varying ?category=/?brand=/?q=/?features= values to mint distinct cache keys
instructions: Authenticate as the store owner and loop create requests with unique names; per-(store,name) uniqueness permits unlimited distinct rows and no count check exists on any path.
For discounts keep is_active=true, starts_at<=now and ends_at=null so every row enters running_discount_stamp/running_discounts_of on every request.
Let public traffic (or self-issued anonymous requests with distinct filter combinations, each producing a unique _params_fingerprint cache key) hit the catalog endpoint.
Observe per-request Discount scans with campaign.is_running() per row, O(products x discounts) pricing on each miss, and response payload growth proportional to taxonomy/discount row counts.
execution.observed_result: Source-verified: every catalog request executes running_discount_stamp (one Discount query + Python loop over all in-window discounts calling campaign.is_running per row) before cache lookup; every cache miss serializes ALL categories/brands including empty ones and ALL running discounts as promotions, and runs effective_pricing_of per product iterating every running discount (O(PxD)). No count validation exists in Category/Brand/Discount create paths, serializers, or models — unlike max_products/SERVICES_MAX/image caps enforced under select_for_update.

remediation.strategy: Bound every owner-writable collection that feeds shared public payloads. Add count quotas for categories, brands and discounts — new plan benefits (e.g., max_categories/max_brands/max_discounts in dict_benefits + dict_plan_benefits) or fixed ceilings like SERVICES_MAX — enforced in create under select_for_update on the store row, mirroring can_add_product/can_add_service (e.g., a can_add_taxonomy/can_add_discount helper checked inside transaction.atomic in each viewset's create). Independently of quotas: exclude categories/brands with products_count=0 from the public payload (or cap the serialized lists), cap the promotions list length, and consider folding the discount stamp into a cached payload version instead of recomputing per request. Optionally dedupe/throttle notify_store_discount on mass discount creation.

    related = {'category': 'categories', 'brand': 'brands', 'discount': 'discounts'}[kind]
    return getattr(store, related).count() < limit

likelihood.reason: Requires a paying tenant running a sustained automated create loop; the 'user' throttle (1000/day) slows accumulation to days-weeks for large row counts, but categories/brands need only the cheapest plan and there is no technical barrier beyond scripting. Public-read amplification needs only anonymous traffic on that store.

impact.reason: Amplifies shared-infrastructure cost (per-request Discount scan, O(PxD) pricing CPU on misses, unbounded payload size) for that store's public catalog and for shared workers/cache. Bounded by PUBLIC_CACHE_TTL=120s, 'public_read' 1000/hour/IP throttle, plan-capped products on lower tiers, and the owner-create throttle. No cross-tenant data exposure, integrity loss, or availability kill demonstrated from source.

confidence.reason: Every link verified directly in current source: absent count validation across viewsets/serializers/models/benefit catalog, per-request running_discount_stamp before cache_get, O(PxD) effective pricing on miss, unfiltered taxonomy/promotions serialization, and the contrasting locked-quota pattern for products and services.

title: Chat payload leaks full staff directory (ids, names/usernames, online presence) to every paying customer despite per-message anonymity
description: The support chat deliberately anonymizes staff in messages — ChatMessageSerializer.get_sender_name returns the constant 'Soporte DAVENT' for from_staff messages (serializers.py:31-37) and the serializer module docstring promises 'nunca emails ni datos de cuenta'. However, SupportChatViewSet.list() and heartbeat() embed staff_roster() in every customer response (viewset.py:105 and viewset.py:198). staff_roster() (services.py:134-147) iterates User.objects.filter(is_staff=True, is_active=True) — i.e., ALL staff and superuser accounts, not just support agents — and returns {id (DB pk), name (get_full_name() or username — a login identifier), online} for each. Any authenticated user with a paid non-trial plan (chat_enabled: suscription.grants_access() and not plan.is_trial, services.py:29-39) can enumerate the complete staff account directory, real names or usernames, primary keys, and real-time per-person presence. The frontend does consume the roster (DashboardView.vue:3379/3426 -> chatStaff -> chatContacts rendered as named team members with online status at lines 6452-6464), so names/online are an intended UI feature — but the backend scope (every is_staff account incl. superusers, username fallback, numeric ids) exceeds what a support-team display needs and contradicts the per-message anonymity boundary.
root_cause: staff_roster() (services.py:140) scopes only by is_staff+is_active with no support-role filter, and both customer-facing responses (viewset.py:105 'staff': staff_roster(), viewset.py:198) include it unconditionally on every list/heartbeat poll.
intended_behavior: Either the roster should be limited to agents actually handling support and return a display-safe label (no login username, no DB id), or — if showing the team is intended product behavior — it should not expose every staff principal including superusers/non-support staff with account ids and real-time presence.

Customer POST /api/chat/heartbeat/ response includes 'staff': staff_roster() on every ~45s presence poll.
User.objects.filter(is_staff=True, is_active=True) — all staff incl. superusers; presence set from ChatPresence (user__is_staff).
Each entry returns {'id': u.id, 'name': u.get_full_name().strip() or u.username, 'online': u.id in online} — DB pk, full name or login username, live presence.
from_staff messages are hardcoded to 'Soporte DAVENT' — per-message anonymity enforced while the roster bypasses it.

evidence.description: staff_roster() docstring claims 'solo id, nombre publico y presencia (nunca email ni datos de cuenta)' but the query is all is_staff users and name falls back to username.
User.objects.filter(is_staff=True, is_active=True) — includes superusers and any staff account, no support-role scoping.
'name': u.get_full_name().strip() or u.username — username is a login credential identifier.
Customer list() embeds 'staff': staff_roster().
Customer heartbeat() embeds 'staff': staff_roster() every poll.
chat_enabled: non-staff requires suscription.grants_access() and not plan.is_trial — paid non-trial plan gate; _gate at viewset.py:76-80 raises 403 otherwise.
get_sender_name returns 'Soporte DAVENT' for staff messages — anonymity enforced per-message.

chatContacts = [BOT_MEMBER, ...chatStaff] — roster rendered as named support-team contacts (lines 6452-6464 show s.name and online status), confirming the feature is consumed; the staff id is only a frontend key and is never sent back (send() uses own thread for non-staff).

conditions.description: Attacker holds an authenticated platform account (JWT Bearer) with a paid non-trial subscription granting chat access; trial and no-plan accounts get 403 (list) or 204 (heartbeat).
Non-staff customer principal — staff callers receive the staff bandeja branch instead and do not get this payload.
Read-only enumeration; no writes required. ChatPresence rows determine the 'online' flags.

execution.attacker_perspective: Paying customer (any paid non-trial plan) calling the support-chat endpoints with their own Bearer token.
instructions: Obtain a paid non-trial plan on a platform account.
GET /api/chat/ (or POST /api/chat/heartbeat/) with the Bearer token.
Read response.staff: a list of {id, name, online} for every active is_staff user — names resolve to full name or login username, ids are DB primary keys, online reflects live ChatPresence.
execution.observed_result: Source-derived: response.staff enumerates every active staff/superuser account with id, display name (full name or username) and real-time online flag; repeated heartbeat polls keep presence fresh. No email is exposed, but usernames (login identifiers) and the complete admin/staff directory are.

remediation.strategy: Scope the roster to support-facing staff only (dedicated flag/group or is_staff AND a support permission), return a display-safe label instead of falling back to username, and drop the numeric id if the UI does not need it — the frontend uses id only as a local key, so a synthetic key or omission suffices. If showing the team is intended product behavior, document it and explicitly exclude superusers/non-support staff and presence granularity.

def staff_roster():
    #Solo agentes de soporte reales: excluir superusers y staff sin rol de
    #soporte; nombre de exhibicion sin fallback a username (identificador
    #de login) y sin exponer el pk — el front lo usa solo como key local.
    since   =   _online_since()
    online  =   set(ChatPresence.objects.filter(user__is_staff = True, last_seen__gte = since).values_list('user_id', flat = True))
    roster  =   []
    for u in User.objects.filter(is_staff = True, is_active = True, is_superuser = False).order_by('first_name', 'username'):
        roster.append({
            'id'        :   u.id,
            'name'      :   (u.get_full_name().strip() or 'Soporte DAVENT'),
            'online'    :   u.id in online,
        })
    roster.sort(key = lambda s: not s['online'])
    return roster

likelihood.reason: Requires a paid non-trial plan (real monetary barrier) and an authenticated account; once obtained, enumeration is a single GET/POST repeated on heartbeat.

impact.reason: Discloses staff names/usernames/DB ids/online presence to customers — aids targeted phishing and credential attacks against admin accounts — but exposes no credentials, emails, or tenant data, and platform login is separately rate-limited.

confidence.reason: All technical facts verified in source (roster query, payload fields, gate, frontend consumption). Residual uncertainty is classification: the frontend deliberately renders a named team roster, so names/online may be intended product behavior; the defensible excess is the unscoped all-staff/superuser coverage, username fallback, and id exposure contradicting the documented anonymity invariant.

title: Django 5.2 GZipMiddleware buffers the entire SSE stream — events and heartbeats only reach the client at ~50s stream close
description: GZipMiddleware is enabled (DaventProject/settings.py:241) and the pinned runtime is Django==5.2.18 (requirements.txt:17), installed verbatim into both deploy images (docker/api/Dockerfile stages builder/runtime; render.yaml uses the same dockerfilePath). Verified against the Django stable/5.2.x release-branch source (the branch 5.2.18 is tagged from; the per-chunk flush fix, PR #20401 merged 2026-03-09, is absent from stable/5.2.x HEAD and therefore from every 5.2.x release): GZipMiddleware.process_response wraps response.streaming_content in compress_sequence whenever the request's Accept-Encoding contains 'gzip' and no Content-Encoding is set — with no content-type exemption, so text/event-stream is compressed. compress_sequence writes each SSE frame via zfile.write() but never calls zfile.flush(); zlib withholds output until its pending buffer reaches ~16-17KB (documented in the Django commit that removed the flush: 'the buffer is being flushed every 17k or so') or until the GzipFile context closes. The stream's frames are tens-to-hundreds of bytes (': conectado', ': ping' every 15s, small JSON events), so for any realistic notification volume NOTHING is emitted — not even response headers, since WSGI sends headers with the first body bytes — until either ~17KB accumulates or the generator ends at STREAM_MAX_SECONDS=50 and the gzip trailer flushes everything at once. Consequence: browsers (which always send Accept-Encoding: gzip on EventSource) receive the whole 50s of events/heartbeats in a single burst at reconnect time; the 'unread'/'notification' events effectively degrade to ~50s polling granularity and the 15s heartbeat cannot serve its liveness purpose. The view's X-Accel-Buffering:no only affects nginx proxy buffering and does not prevent Django-side gzip; nginx gzip_types excludes text/event-stream so nginx neither re-compresses nor helps; Caddy has no encode directive and passes the upstream Content-Encoding:gzip through.
root_cause: django.middleware.gzip.GZipMiddleware unconditionally gzip-compresses sync streaming responses via django.utils.text.compress_sequence, and in Django 5.2.x compress_sequence performs zfile.write() per chunk without zfile.flush(), so zlib buffers the stream until ~17KB pending or close — defeating the real-time delivery contract of text/event-stream.
intended_behavior: SSE responses must reach the wire per chunk. Either bypass compression for text/event-stream (skip GZipMiddleware for that content type / set an explicit identity encoding the middleware respects) or run a Django version whose compress_sequence flushes per chunk (fix present on main/6.0 line; verify 5.2.x backport status before upgrading).

trace.description: 'django.middleware.gzip.GZipMiddleware' enabled for all responses including the SSE stream

StreamingHttpResponse(self._events(...), content_type='text/event-stream'); sets Cache-Control:no-cache and X-Accel-Buffering:no (nginx-only hint) but NO Content-Encoding — so GZipMiddleware will compress it for gzip-accepting clients

for response.streaming (sync): response.streaming_content = compress_sequence(response.streaming_content, ...) whenever re_accepts_gzip matches HTTP_ACCEPT_ENCODING and no Content-Encoding header exists — no content-type check exempts text/event-stream

for item in sequence: zfile.write(item); data = buf.read(); yield if data — NO zfile.flush() per chunk; zlib emits only at ~16-17KB pending or at GzipFile.__exit__ (stream close at ~50s) → entire SSE session buffered into one burst

evidence.description: GZipMiddleware present in MIDDLEWARE
Django==5.2.18 — the pinned runtime for both deploy paths
pip install --no-index -r requirements.txt → deployed Django is exactly 5.2.18 (compose api/celery/migrate and Render docker runtime alike)
response['X-Accel-Buffering']='no' — disables nginx proxy buffering only; does not set Content-Encoding, so Django gzip still applies
proxy_read_timeout 60s — upstream silence for ~50s stays under the limit, so the buffered stream still completes (barely)
nginx gzip_types excludes text/event-stream — nginx does not gzip SSE itself, but passes through the upstream Content-Encoding:gzip unchanged

[django/utils/text.py (Django 5.2.x stable branch, == requirements pin)] compress_sequence lacks zfile.flush() per chunk — verified on the stable/5.2.x release branch; upstream fix PR django/django#20401 (ticket #36293, 'buffer is being flushed every 17k or so') merged 2026-03-09 is absent from stable/5.2.x HEAD

[django/middleware/gzip.py (Django 5.2.x stable branch)] process_response wraps sync streaming_content in compress_sequence with no content-type exemption; requires only 'gzip' in Accept-Encoding (sent by all browsers for EventSource)

conditions.description: GZipMiddleware enabled (default in this repo) and client sends Accept-Encoding:gzip — true for every browser EventSource; non-gzip clients (e.g. curl without --compressed) bypass compression entirely and see correct streaming.

Typical notification volume keeps each 50s stream well under ~17KB of SSE frames, so nothing flushes before close; a burst >~17KB (e.g. large catch-up payloads) could emit mid-stream but events still arrive late and batched.
Buffered upstream silence lasts until ~50s stream end; nginx proxy_read_timeout is 60s so the response still completes — headroom is only ~10s.

execution.attacker_perspective: Not attacker-driven — a deterministic defect affecting every legitimate SSE client.
payloads: GET /api/customer/notifications/stream/?ticket=<T>&store=<slug> with Accept-Encoding: gzip (default browser EventSource behavior)
instructions: 1. Open the stream as the SPA does (EventSource → ticket → GET stream).

2. Trigger or wait for a customer notification; observe that no 'notification'/'unread' event arrives in real time — all buffered frames plus the final 'bye' are delivered in one burst when the generator closes at ~50s.
3. Confirm response headers (Content-Encoding:gzip) arrive only with that first burst, since WSGI emits headers with the first non-empty body chunk.
execution.observed_result: Source-traced: middleware chain, pinned-version library code on the release branch, and the absence of any Content-Encoding/content-type bypass prove the buffering path; the ~17KB zlib threshold is documented by Django developers in the fix commit. Not observed on a live instance (source-only review; no venv present in the workspace to byte-inspect the installed package — the stable/5.2.x branch source stands in for the 5.2.18 wheel).

remediation.strategy: Exempt text/event-stream from gzip compression: replace 'django.middleware.gzip.GZipMiddleware' with a subclass that returns the response untouched when Content-Type starts with 'text/event-stream' (the Django ticket itself recommends this), or set an explicit no-op Content-Encoding the middleware respects. Alternatively/Additionally upgrade Django once the compress_sequence flush fix is backported to the deployed 5.2.x line (fix is on main; verify release notes). The heartbeat/liveness design then works as intended and events arrive per chunk.

likelihood.reason: Deterministic for every gzip-accepting client — i.e. every real browser running the SPA's EventSource; no attacker action or special config needed.

impact.reason: Customer notifications degrade from push to ~50s batched delivery and heartbeats cannot serve liveness; a security-adjacent timeliness defect, not a trust-boundary crossing — data still arrives, just late, and the 50s<60s timeout margins keep streams alive.

confidence.reason: Full code path proven from repo source plus the pinned Django 5.2.x release-branch source of gzip.py/text.py (no local venv exists to byte-inspect the installed wheel, and no live instance was tested per constraints). Residual uncertainty is limited to the exact zlib emission threshold — immaterial, since any threshold ≫ SSE frame size produces the same buffer-until-close outcome — and to whether a future 5.2.x backport changes the picture (irrelevant: the pin is ==5.2.18).

title: Stream ticket is a replayable, session-unbound bearer credential transmitted in the URL query (120s window)
description: The SSE credential is signing.dumps({'c': customer_pk, 's': slug}, salt='customer-notifications-stream') verified with max_age=TICKET_TTL=120. Verified sub-claims: (1) REPLAYABLE — the payload carries no jti/nonce and nothing is consumed at verify time, so one ticket authorizes unlimited concurrent stream connections for its full 120s TTL (this is also the multiplier that makes customers-sse:worker-exhaustion cheap). title: Single customer account + single IP can saturate all gunicorn gthreads via replayable SSE tickets (full-API DoS)
description: GET /api/customer/notifications/stream/ is AllowAny and authenticated solely by a replayable signed ticket, throttled only by CustomerPublicReadThrottle (scope 'public_read' = 1000/hour per IP). Each SSE connection consumes exactly one throttle token at check_throttles time and then occupies one gunicorn gthread for up to STREAM_MAX_SECONDS=50s (bounded below only by client disconnect, detected on the next ≤15s ping write). The whole API shares workers=3 × threads=4 = 12 concurrent request handlers (docker/api/gunicorn.conf.py:14-16; compose/.env.example 3×4, Render blueprint 2×4=8 — even easier). Sustained saturation needs ~N×3600/50 connection-opens/hour (864 for 12 threads, 576 for 8) — inside the 1000/hour per-IP budget with ~14-42% headroom, and a fresh burst of up to 1000 requests is allowed instantly by the sliding-window throttle. Because tickets carry no jti (customers-sse:ticket-replay-no-epoch), ONE ticket authorizes unlimited concurrent streams during its 120s TTL; ~720 ticket-mints/day per account covers continuous operation, under the 'user'=1000/day stream-ticket budget — so a single self-registered customer account (registration issues a working JWT immediately, email_verified not required) plus one source IP suffices for indefinite full-API denial of service for every tenant, storefront, auth endpoint and admin path.
root_cause: The SSE endpoint was given the generic public-read throttle (1000/hour/IP, sized for cheap request/response reads) instead of a bound proportional to connection-hold cost: a stream request is not a read, it is a 50-second worker-thread lease. No per-customer/per-IP concurrent-stream counter exists, and the ticket's replayability within its 120s TTL makes per-connection credential cost ~zero.
intended_behavior: A long-lived connection endpoint must bound concurrent holds, not just request rate: a dedicated throttle scope sized for the feature plus a cache-backed in-flight counter (e.g. max 2-4 open streams per customer+IP), single-use or near-single-use tickets, and/or an nginx limit_conn on the stream route.

title: Feed customer writes (comment/like/vote) are completely unthrottled — FeedWriteThrottle is an AnonRateThrottle that skips authenticated customers
description: All three customer write endpoints of the store feed — POST /api/stores/public/<slug>/feed/<pk>/comments/, .../like/, .../vote/ — declare FeedWriteThrottle (scope 'store_review', configured 10/hour in settings, intended as antispam). title: Django admin unreachable through the VPS web tier for any ADMIN_URL not under /admin/ or /api/ — obfuscation requirement and proxy coverage contradict each other
description: The compose/VPS deploy requires ADMIN_URL to be non-predictable: users.E001 fails check --deploy for 'admin/', the CI preflight greps it out (ci-cd.yml:483-487), and DEPLOY_CHECK_STRICT=1 aborts boot. title: Caddy edge image builds caddy-dns/cloudflare plugin at unpinned latest — mutable build input into the TLS terminator for all traffic
description: docker/caddy/Dockerfile runs `xcaddy build --with github.com/caddy-dns/cloudflare --replace golang.org/x/net=golang.org/x/net@v0.62.0`. The --replace pins x/net, but the cloudflare plugin module itself has no @version — xcaddy resolves the latest commit of the module repo at image-build time and produces the caddy binary that becomes the production edge: it terminates TLS for the platform wildcard AND on-demand TLS for every verified customer custom domain, holds CF_API_TOKEN (Zone.DNS), and proxies all HTTP. Any writer to that upstream repo (or a compromised module resolution path before sumdb pinning — xcaddy generates a fresh go.mod without a committed go.sum) can land code in the next scheduled/CI image build -> rebuild -> deploy to the edge with full MITM capability over every request including admin sessions and customer PII. Base images caddy:2-builder/caddy:2 are also tag-mutable. Same class, lower trust: compose `docker compose pull` (ci-cd.yml:513) re-pulls tag-mutable postgres:16-alpine and redis:7.4-alpine on every deploy.
root_cause: Build input (VCS module + base image tags) not bound to an immutable version/digest; no go.sum committed for the xcaddy module set.
intended_behavior: Pin the plugin to a release tag/commit (@vX.Y.Z or pseudo-version), commit the resulting go.mod/go.sum or build via a locked module file, and digest-pin base images (or rely on Dependabot docker updates with review).

title: DEBUG=True reachable in production via non-'True' env spellings — every deploy guard compares raw strings while decouple cast=bool accepts 'true'/'1'/'yes'/'on'
description: Three independent gates try to keep DEBUG off in production and all three compare the raw env string, not the parsed boolean: (1) docker/api/entrypoint.sh runs `check --deploy` only `if [ "$DEBUG" != "True" ]`; (2) the CI deploy preflight greps `^DEBUG=True` case-sensitively; (3) every custom security check (DaventProject/checks.py project.E001-E005, envguard E006-E018 prod rules, users.E001-E003) early-returns or is skipped when settings.DEBUG is true. But settings.py parses `DEBUG = config('DEBUG', default=False, cast=bool)` and python-decouple's bool cast uses strtobool semantics (verified by executing the repo venv: 'true','TRUE','1','yes','on','t','y' all -> True). So DEBUG=true/1/yes/TRUE/on in .env or the Render dashboard yields settings.DEBUG=True while the entrypoint still runs check --deploy — which passes vacuously because all project checks return [] under DEBUG and Django's own deploy findings are warnings below --fail-level ERROR — and the CI grep misses it entirely. urls.py then mounts /api/auth/ (api-auth/), /api/schema/, swagger, redoc, and static(MEDIA_URL): the last serves MEDIA_ROOT including private/ chat attachments on deployments without the nginx /media/private/ 404 (Render). Technical 500/404 pages also expose tracebacks. SECURE_* cookie/HSTS defaults flip to insecure under DEBUG, though both documented deploys pin them explicitly via compose/render.yaml env, mitigating that specific downgrade.
root_cause: Boolean security gates implemented as exact/case-sensitive shell string comparisons (`[ "$DEBUG" != "True" ]`, `grep '^DEBUG=True'`) instead of comparing the parsed settings.DEBUG, while the settings parser (python-decouple cast=bool -> strtobool) accepts a family of truthy spellings. intended_behavior: Any env spelling that Django parses as DEBUG=True must be treated identically by the entrypoint gate, the CI preflight, and a system check — production must refuse to boot (or at minimum run a check that can actually fail) whenever the effective DEBUG is true.

title: RequestIdMiddleware logs raw request.path — percent-encoded control chars forge log lines
description: RequestIdMiddleware.__call__ ends every request with logger.info('request id=%s %s %s -> %s (%.0fms)', ..., request.method, request.path, ...). request.path is the URL-decoded PATH_INFO; a request like GET /%0AForged%20log%20entry HTTP/1.1 yields a newline inside the logged path, splitting one access-log record into attacker-shaped lines in stdout (json-file logs on the VPS, Render logs). The incoming X-Request-ID is charset-validated (middleware.py:120-123) but request.path is not, and the ScrubSecretsFilter redacts secret patterns only — it has no control-character stripping (logscrub.py:16-25). nginx proxy_pass forwards the raw request URI and gunicorn unquotes %XX into PATH_INFO per WSGI convention, so the encoded control char survives to Django.

intended_behavior: Log fields derived from request data should be single-line sanitized (strip/replace [\x00-\x1f\x7f]) before emission.

description: /sitemap.xml is public and unauthenticated wherever Django serves it. title: Authenticated users bypass the content_report throttle entirely — unbounded report emails to the legal mailbox
description: POST /api/content-reports/ is AllowAny and every valid create enqueues a Celery task that sends an email to LEGAL_REPORTS_EMAIL. The dedicated anti-spam throttle (scope 'content_report', 5/hour per IP) is implemented as ContentReportRateThrottle(AnonRateThrottle) at AdminApp/domains/legal/views/viewset_base.py:14-18. DRF's AnonRateThrottle.get_cache_key() returns None whenever request.user.is_authenticated (venv/Lib/site-packages/rest_framework/throttling.py:173-180) and SimpleRateThrottle.allow_request returns True when the key is None (throttling.py:119-121). Worse than the hunter claimed: ContentReportBaseViewSet.throttle_classes = [ContentReportRateThrottle] (viewset_base.py:25) REPLACES DRF's DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES (settings.py:75-78: ResilientAnonRateThrottle + ResilientUserRateThrottle), so for an authenticated caller NO rate limit applies at all — not even the 'user' 1000/day fallback the hunter assumed. JWTAuthentication is the default auth class (settings.py:64-66) and DRF authenticates before permission checks, so a valid Bearer token on the AllowAny endpoint fully populates request.user. The frontend itself sends the platform Bearer on this endpoint (legal.api.js uses http.js whose interceptor attaches Authorization when a session token exists, http.js:116-124). Result: any registered account (free registration, no plan required) can submit an unlimited number of valid reports — each creating a ContentReport row, a Celery task, and an email to LEGAL_REPORTS_EMAIL — completely defeating the 5/hour bound that settings.py:132-134 documents as the anti-email-bombing control.
root_cause: ContentReportRateThrottle subclasses AnonRateThrottle (viewset_base.py:14-18), which is anonymous-only by design, and it is installed via throttle_classes which overrides the project's default throttle set. For authenticated requests get_cache_key() returns None so the throttle silently allows everything, and because the viewset replaces DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES no other throttle (anon 100/day, user 1000/day) covers the gap.
intended_behavior: The 5/hour 'content_report' limit should bound every caller of the public create endpoint — anonymous and authenticated alike — since every accepted POST produces an email to LEGAL_REPORTS_EMAIL plus a DB row and Celery/SMTP work.

title: Any paid plan price satisfies the payment amount check — pay the cheapest tier price, receive the most expensive plan for 30 days
description: CreatePaymentQuery validates an MP payment's transaction_amount against `accepted_amounts`, which is the UNION of every non-trial plan price plus pending_charge — not the amount corresponding to the entitlement actually being granted. A payment whose amount equals ANY plan's price is accepted and ApplyPendingPlanQuery then applies whatever pending_plan_suscription (or the already-rewritten plan_suscription of a pending_payment subscription) is set, granting the most expensive plan while collecting the cheapest plan's price. The broad acceptance was added deliberately to avoid orphaned MP charges when a preference/debit was issued before a plan change (services.py:107-112 comments), but it decouples amount from entitlement in both directions. Verified deterministic exploit: (a) pending_payment subscription — create checkout preference at cheap plan, PATCH plan_suscription to expensive (PENDING_PAYMENT branch rewrites plan_suscription directly), pay the stale cheap preference -> expensive plan ACTIVE 30d; (b) active subscription — create checkout preference at current cheap plan price, then request upgrade to expensive plan (pending_plan + prorated pending_charge via RequestPlanChangeQuery), pay the stale cheap preference -> paid_amount != pending_charge so prorated=False -> pending expensive plan applied AND end_date renewed +30d. Repeatable monthly via the stale-preference cycle or a failed best-effort UpdatePreapprovalPlanQuery realignment (RequestPlanChangeQuery swallows MP errors). IssueInvoiceQuery then emits a fiscally inconsistent invoice: plan_name snapshot = expensive plan, total = cheap payment.amount.
root_cause: AdminApp/domains/payments/services/services.py CreatePaymentQuery lines 115-124: `accepted_amounts` unions {pending_plan-or-current price, current plan price, ALL SuscriptionPlan prices where is_trial=False, pending_charge} and only checks set membership — the granted entitlement (pending_plan or pending_payment plan_suscription) is never bound to the amount paid. `expected_amount` (line 106) is computed but used only in the error message. ApplyPendingPlanQuery (lines 281-313) applies pending_plan whenever a payment is APPROVED with renew=True; the only amount-sensitive gate is `paid_amount == pending_charge` deciding prorated-vs-full-renewal, never amount-vs-plan-price.
intended_behavior: A payment should only credit the entitlement its amount pays for: pending_charge for prorated upgrades, or the price of the specific plan being applied (pending_plan if set else plan_suscription for pending_payment). Stale-amount MP charges should either map amount->plan (grant the plan that amount corresponds to) or be rejected/flagged for reconciliation — as the sibling StoreApp storepayments webhook does (exact order.total match required, mismatch -> manual review) — rather than silently upgrading entitlement.

An earlier preference keeps its creation-time amount and stays payable.
Lines 382-391 freeze unit_price + external_reference into the MP Checkout Pro preference — the charged amount is immutable once issued; MP preferences remain payable at the snapshot price.

PATCH /api/suscriptions/<id>/ {plan_suscription}: PENDING_PAYMENT branch (lines 74-83) rewrites plan_suscription directly to the expensive plan; ACTIVE branch (line 90) -> RequestPlanChangeQuery sets pending_plan_suscription=expensive + pending_charge=prorated.

Lines 132-135: upgrade sets pending_plan_suscription=target_plan and pending_charge=_upgrade_charge(...) (prorated); downgrade sets pending_plan only. Live-preapproval realignment is best-effort — exceptions swallowed at lines 136-141, so MP can keep debiting the old amount.

Lines 287-313: pending_plan applied to plan_suscription unconditionally on APPROVED; prorated gate (281-286) requires paid_amount == pending_charge exactly, so any other accepted amount -> prorated=False -> end_date = now+30d, status=ACTIVE, period_payment_id=payment. Expensive plan granted at cheap-tier price.

PENDING_PAYMENT branch rewrites plan_suscription directly (lines 79-82) — no pending_plan indirection, so a stale cheap preference pays for whatever plan is currently set.
UpdatePreapprovalPlanQuery realignment is best-effort inside try/except — a failed MP update leaves the preapproval debiting the old cheap amount, recurring the mismatch monthly.

Seeded plans differ in price — 25000/30000/40000/60000 ARS — giving a real spread for the cheapest-to-most-expensive arbitrage.

title: Pattern preview is a bounded per-request render already constrained by the global authenticated user throttle; absent dedicated scope/cache is hardening, not a demonstrated DoS
description: Verified the request path: GET /api/design/patterns/<slug>/preview/ is a detail action on DesignCatalogViewSet. get_throttles only special-cases action 'default' to PublicReadThrottle; preview falls through to DRF DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES (ResilientAnonRateThrottle + ResilientUserRateThrottle). For an authenticated caller AnonRateThrottle returns no key and UserRateThrottle keys on request.user.pk with DEFAULT_THROTTLE_RATES['user']='1000/day'. There is no dedicated preview scope and no server-side preview cache (catalog_cached is used only for catalog/default payloads). The render itself is bounded: DesignPatternSerializer validates html/css/js to CODE_MAX=200_000 chars each, preview_pattern uses a fixed small sample context and constant sample fragments, sanitizes markup/css, and returns at most the stored markup size plus bounded theme CSS — there is no DB fan-out, external call, cache-stamp amplification, or output multiplier. The frontend calls the endpoint on demand from the picker. A dedicated throttle/cache would be defense-in-depth, but source does not show a trust-boundary violation or a meaningful amplification: the endpoint is authenticated, globally rate-limited per user, input-bounded, and cost-bounded.
claimed_root_cause: Pattern preview performs a server-side render on every request with only the global user throttle (1000/day) and no dedicated throttle scope or cache, so it is claimed to be an unbounded/under-throttled render cost.

ResilientAnonRateThrottle + ResilientUserRateThrottle with 'anon':'100/day', 'user':'1000/day', 'public_read':'1000/hour'; no 'design_preview' or similar scope exists.
Authenticated requests key the 'user' scope by request.user.pk; anonymous requests fall back to IP. ResilientUserRateThrottle only adds fail-open cache behavior (DaventProject/throttling.py:91-96).
CODE_MAX=200_000 and validate_html/css/js bound each stored markup field; variables are sanitized by clean_pattern_variables and render escapes non-list values (models.py:358-380).

Per-request render uses fixed SAMPLE_PRODUCTS/CATEGORIES/SERVICES, sanitize_markup(pattern.render(sample_context(), raw=raw)), theme_css+SURFACE_CSS+pattern.css through sanitize_css, and returns raw pattern.js; cost is proportional to bounded stored markup, not to request count beyond the 1000/day/user cap.

evidence.description: preview action has no throttle_classes and no cache; it is the only per-request markup render endpoint in the design viewset.
catalog_cached() exists for catalog/default payloads only; preview does not use it, confirming the 'no cache' observation but also showing cache is not part of the catalog contract.
_ResilientThrottleMixin fails open on cache errors; ResilientUserRateThrottle is the class actually applied to authenticated preview requests.
Sample context is constant and small (8 products, 5 categories, 4 services); no tenant data or unbounded query is rendered.
openPatternPreview calls designApi.patternPreview once per user-initiated 'Ver este diseño' click; there is no automatic polling or fan-out.
validate_html/css/js enforce CODE_MAX=200_000 per field, bounding single-request input size.

reason: The observation (no dedicated throttle scope/cache) is accurate but does not establish a security issue. The endpoint is authenticated, inherits a concrete per-user rate limit (1000/day keyed by user.pk), accepts only bounded markup fields (200k chars each), renders a constant sample context, sanitizes output, and has no amplification fan-out or cache-stamp cost. Whether 1000 renders/day is operationally meaningful depends on deployment capacity and account-creation economics — runtime facts — but even granting them, this remains an authenticated API within the platform's normal throttling budget rather than a trust-boundary violation. Recommendation is hardening only: add a dedicated throttle scope and/or cache keyed by pattern revision+theme+style if profiling shows preview cost matters.

title: sync/run reaches publish_design_draft without a direct has_customization gate, but draft writes are gated and public render/serializer re-filter — no unauthorized effective publish
description: Verified the plumbing: POST /api/stores/sync/run/ resolves only the caller's own Store (user__user=request.user) and calls run_sync, which calls publish_design_draft when design_draft_pending. Unlike customization_publish/discard/restore and the customization PATCH, sync_run and the sync GET have no profile_has_benefit check. publish_design_draft copies layout_config_draft->layout_config and site_theme_draft->site_theme verbatim and only re-checks template_draft against allowed_templates_of before publishing. The claimed impact is nevertheless refuted on current source. (1) Owner-scoped: no cross-store IDOR. (2) Drafts are not freely writable: customization PATCH requires has_customization and validates layout_config via clean_layout_config and site_theme via clean_site_theme against current benefits; AI-design apply requires has_customization+has_ai_design and cleans layout before writing drafts. (3) Plan coupling: every seeded plan sets has_public_link=True together with has_customization=True, and plan_benefits_of returns {} unless suscription.grants_access(), so an expired/inactive subscription yields no benefits and the public endpoint 404s on has_public_link while allowed_templates_of collapses to ('raiz',). (4) Even if a stale premium draft is published, the public read path re-filters: StoreCustomizationPublicSerializer.to_representation runs filter_site_theme by current has_design_plus/has_design_advanced/has_customization and recomputes site_templates/show_catalog; the public store endpoint requires has_public_link; render_store_pattern re-checks template and site_theme.style.id against allowed_templates_of; and layout_config's premium/ai_only blocks are inert because clean_layout_config drops them at write time and the live frontend templateBlocks() only overlays saved values onto canonical template blocks (non-canonical ids are dropped). The prior catalog layout read-drift candidate was already rejected for exactly this dead-sink reason. The missing has_customization check on sync_run/sync GET is a real consistency/defense-in-depth gap, but it does not produce a demonstrated unauthorized public change under the shipped plan catalog.

reason: The missing direct has_customization check on sync_run (and the read-only sync GET) is a genuine consistency gap worth hardening, but the claimed security impact does not hold on current source. The path is owner-scoped; every shipped plan couples has_public_link with has_customization; an inactive/expired subscription yields no benefits and the public web 404s; draft mutations are only reachable through has_customization/has_ai_design-gated writes that sanitize layout_config/site_theme; publish_design_draft still re-checks template_draft against the live plan whitelist; and the public serializer/render path re-filters theme, templates, and pattern selection while non-canonical/premium layout blocks are inert in the live renderer. A residual would require an out-of-catalog plan granting has_public_link without has_customization or direct DB manipulation — an admin/config anomaly, not a source-proven trust-boundary violation.

title: Inventory denial and merchant spam via soft stock-reservation abuse across self-registered customer accounts
description: End-to-end source-verified abuse chain: (1) POST /api/customer-auth/register/ is AllowAny self-service registration guarded only by CustomerRegisterThrottle (scope 'register' = 10/hour keyed by client IP when no customer session exists) with NO captcha — CustomerRegisterView.post never calls verify_captcha, and CustomerRegisterSerializer only requires a unique well-formed email plus a Django-policy password. RegisterCustomerQuery creates the Customer with model defaults is_active=True / email_verified=False and _session_response issues a working customer_access JWT immediately; email verification is never required anywhere in the order path (IsCustomer checks only isinstance+is_active; mails.py:269-272 only skips CUSTOMER lifecycle emails for unverified addresses). (2) POST /api/stores/public/<slug>/orders/ requires only IsCustomer and is throttled by OrderCreateThrottle — a ResilientUserRateThrottle (scope 'store_order_create', rate '10/hour') whose DRF UserRateThrottle.get_cache_key keys on request.user.pk = customer.pk, i.e. PER ACCOUNT, not per IP. One IP minting ~10 accounts/hour therefore yields ~100 orders/hour. (3) The order captcha is deterministic arithmetic (add/sub/mul of small ints, single-use nonce, 5 attempts, >=3s min delay) — a scriptable speed bump, not a bot barrier. (4) Each created order claims SOFT STOCK globally: claimed_quantities sums OrderItem.qty over ALL customers' orders with status=PENDING_PAYMENT and expires_at > now (no customer filter), and _resolve_lines rejects any buyer whose qty exceeds product.stock - claimed. Caps are MAX_QTY=100 per product line and MAX_ITEMS=50 lines per order, so a single order can claim up to 100 units of up to 50 SKUs. expires_at = now + payment_deadline_hours (default 48h, owner-configurable 1..720h via StorePaymentConfig serializer); release is TIME-BASED inside the claimed_quantities query (expires_at__gt=now) — it does NOT depend on the expire_orders cron, refuting the hunter's cron blocker. Sustaining the DoS needs only continuous re-ordering at 10/h/account. (5) Every order fires append_event('created') -> dispatch_order_event: 'created' is in OWNER_NOTIFY_KINDS (synchronous in-app Notification to the store owner) and OWNER_EVENT_KINDS (transaction.on_commit -> Celery -> _owner_new_order_mail SMTP). ~100 fake orders/hour/IP = ~100 owner emails+notifications per hour. Impact: a single scripted IP can keep any stock-controlled low-stock SKU permanently 'sold out' to legitimate buyers (qty > available -> ValidationError 'Stock insuficiente') and spam the merchant's inbox/notifications, at zero cost (orders just expire unpaid).
root_cause: Stock reservations are claimed per-order GLOBALLY (claimed_quantities counts every customer's PENDING_PAYMENT orders regardless of owner) while order creation is gated only by a per-customer-pk throttle (10/hour), a scriptable arithmetic captcha, and self-service registration that is itself only IP-throttled at 10/hour with no captcha and no email_verified requirement — there is no per-IP order throttle, no per-store pending-reservation cap, and no verified-principal requirement before stock claims materialize.
intended_behavior: Stock claims should require a minimally verified principal (e.g., email_verified) and/or orders should be throttled per-IP in addition to per-account, with a cap on simultaneous PENDING_PAYMENT reservations per store/customer, so anonymous-scale account minting cannot monopolize inventory or flood the merchant.

trace.description: POST /api/customer-auth/register/ — AllowAny self-service registration; throttle_classes=[CustomerRegisterThrottle] (line 229) = scope 'register' 10/hour (settings.py:111) keyed by IP via CustomerRateThrottle.get_cache_key fallback to get_ident when request.customer is None (lines 175-178). No captcha anywhere in the view (post at 231-246).

POST /api/stores/public/<slug>/orders/ — permission_classes=[IsCustomer] only; throttle_classes=[OrderCreateThrottle] (line 125) = ResilientUserRateThrottle scope 'store_order_create' rate '10/hour' (lines 63-67) keyed by request.user.pk = customer.pk via DRF UserRateThrottle.get_cache_key (venv rest_framework/throttling.py:193-202) — per ACCOUNT, not per IP. Captcha verified at line 136 (arithmetic, scriptable).
Requires only isinstance(request.customer, Customer) and customer.is_active — no email_verified, no membership, no per-store check anywhere in the order path.

Sums OrderItem.qty over Order.status=PENDING_PAYMENT AND order.expires_at__gt=now for the given product_ids across ALL customers (lines 286-294) — one global reservation pool; expiry is evaluated in the query, so release does not depend on the expire_orders cron.

available = product.stock - claimed.get(pid, 0); qty > available -> ValidationError — attacker's pending orders exhaust stock for every other buyer. Caps MAX_QTY=100/line, MAX_ITEMS=50 lines (lines 88-89); expires_at = now + payment_deadline_hours, default 48h, owner-set 1..720h (line 464).

Every 'created' event: kind in OWNER_NOTIFY_KINDS -> synchronous in-app owner Notification (lines 35-38, 89-92) AND kind in OWNER_EVENT_KINDS -> transaction.on_commit Celery email -> mails.py:46-49,276-283 _owner_new_order_mail — fake orders spam the merchant inbox and panel.

evidence.description: 'register': '10/hour' — the only gate on self-service customer account minting; keyed by IP for anonymous requests.
CustomerRegisterThrottle scope='register'; get_cache_key (175-178) uses customer.pk if present else IP ident — anonymous registration buckets per IP at 10/h.

OrderCreateThrottle: ResilientUserRateThrottle scope='store_order_create' rate='10/hour' — DRF UserRateThrottle keys authenticated requests by request.user.pk = customer.pk (per account, evadable by minting accounts).
is_active default True, email_verified default False (line 62); is_authenticated property returns True (117-119) so the customer JWT always takes the pk-keyed throttle path.

RegisterCustomerQuery creates the Customer with model defaults and only enqueues a verification email post-commit — tokens are issued immediately (auth_views.py:246 _session_response); nothing requires email_verified to order.
_captcha_question generates deterministic arithmetic (add/sub/mul of small integers); verify_captcha (76-121) enforces only signature+TTL 300s+min 3s+5 attempts — trivially scriptable.
claimed_quantities filter: product_id__in + order__status=PENDING_PAYMENT + order__expires_at__gt=now — NO customer/store-claimant partition; global soft reservation.
available = product.stock - claimed; qty > available -> ValidationError 'Stock insuficiente' — cross-customer stock monopolization.
expires_at = now + deadline_hours (default 48h via DEFAULT_DEADLINE_HOURS line 90; owner-configurable 1..720h per storepayments/serializers/serializers.py:80-83).
OWNER_NOTIFY_KINDS and OWNER_EVENT_KINDS both contain 'created' — every fake order creates an in-app owner notification plus a Celery-queued owner email (mails.py:276-283).

conditions.description: Target store is published with orders_enabled and has stock-controlled products (product.stock not null); low stock makes monopolization cheap — one order can claim up to 100 units of each of up to 50 SKUs.

Register throttle is per-IP (10/h) and order throttle per-account (10/h): a single IP yields ~10 accounts/h -> ~100 orders/h; IP rotation scales linearly. _pinned_ident (throttling.py:14-27) pins REMOTE_ADDR into the bucket so XFF spoofing does not reset it.

Throttles fail open on cache loss (deliberate, throttling.py:64-79) — but the configured 10/h rates already permit the abuse, so enforcement status does not gate exploitability; fail-open only increases attacker throughput.
The owner-email sub-impact requires a running Celery worker + reachable SMTP; the inventory-denial impact is synchronous DB state inside create_order and needs neither.

execution.attacker_perspective: Anonymous internet user running a script against a public DAVENT store with ecommerce orders enabled.
payloads: POST /api/stores/public/<slug>/orders/ {"items":[{"product_id":<pid>,"qty":<stock>}],"shipping_method":"pickup","payment_method":"transfer","challenge_id":"<id>","captcha_answer":"<answer>"} -> 201 (repeat <=10/h per account, rotate accounts at 10/h per IP)
instructions: Enumerate stock-controlled products and their stock via the public catalog endpoints.
Register customer accounts at 10/hour per IP (no captcha; unique disposable emails suffice; session tokens issued immediately).
For each account, fetch an order captcha, wait >=3s, solve the arithmetic question, and POST orders claiming qty=stock for target SKUs (up to 50 lines x 100 units per order).

Repeat continuously: claims last until expires_at (48h default, up to 720h owner-set) and auto-release via expires_at__gt=now — sustained ~10 orders/h/account keeps low-stock SKUs 'sold out' indefinitely.
Observe legitimate buyers receiving 'Stock insuficiente' ValidationErrors and the owner receiving an in-app notification + email per fake order.
execution.observed_result: Source-derived (read-only audit, not executed): every link verified line-by-line — uncaptcha'd IP-throttled registration, per-customer.pk 10/h order throttle, global claimed_quantities across all customers' PENDING_PAYMENT orders, expires_at-based release independent of cron, and per-order owner notification+email dispatch.

remediation.strategy: Gate stock-claiming order creation on a verified principal and bound abuse per origin: (a) require customer.email_verified (or an equivalent verified-contact check) in PublicOrderCreateView/create_order before materializing claims; (b) add a per-IP order throttle alongside the per-account one so account minting does not multiply the budget; (c) cap simultaneous PENDING_PAYMENT reservations per store and/or per customer (e.g., reject create_order when the customer already holds >=N pending orders for the store, and/or when store-wide pending claims exceed a fraction of stock); (d) add captcha (or disposable-email checks) to customer registration; (e) optionally digest owner 'created' notifications/emails instead of one per order.

likelihood.reason: Fully scriptable end-to-end from a single IP (~10 accounts/h -> ~100 orders/h; each order claims up to 100 units x 50 SKUs, so even one account can exhaust low-stock SKUs). Requires a target store with stock-controlled products worth attacking and sustained automation, but cost and skill barrier are minimal.

impact.reason: Blocks legitimate purchase of targeted SKUs for the attack duration (claims auto-release at expires_at <=720h, default 48h, but the attacker sustains with continuous orders) and floods the merchant with order notifications/emails (~100/h/IP). Bounded per store, reversible, no confidentiality/integrity breach or payment fraud.

confidence.reason: Every link re-verified line-by-line in current source. The hunter's three blockers dissolve on inspection: stock release is expires_at-based inside the claimed_quantities query (checkout.py:290), not cron-dependent; the captcha is provably deterministic arithmetic (contact.py:49-65); throttle rates and cache keys are source constants, and the deliberate fail-open only increases attacker throughput rather than gating the abuse.

title: Plan-gate bypass: store owner address leaks via pattern documents and /r/maps/ redirect on plans without has_location_map
description: StorePublicSerializer.get_location_address correctly requires customization.show_location AND profile_has_benefit(user,'has_location_map') AND user.address (serializers.py:800-817), but two other anonymous public surfaces re-derive the same PII without the benefit check. (1) pattern_render.build_store_context sets address = user.address whenever customization.show_location is true (pattern_render.py:1145) — no has_location_map check — and exposes it as store_address (:1172) plus store_maps_url = contact_redirect_path(store,'maps') (:1172/:1182); _page_flags 'location' (:236) and the flags_css hiding (:1818-1821) key only on show_*, never on plan. DesignPattern.render (design/models/models.py:358-380) substitutes {{store_address}} into the HTML served by GET /api/stores/public/<slug>/pattern/document/ and /pattern/; ~16 sources/*.html templates interpolate it, including 'esencial' — the platform DEFAULT_PATTERN (seed.py:56) and a tier-'base' pattern allowed on Plan basico. (2) contact_redirect_url kind=='maps' (contact.py:162-173) builds https://maps.google.com/?q=<user.address>,<city>,<province> from raw UserProfile.address with zero gates — it does not even check show_location — and is reachable via public_contact (viewset.py:689-711) which only requires is_published+is_blocked+has_public_link. Compounding: show_location defaults True (models.py:243) and the customization PATCH discards LOCATION_FIELDS=('show_location',) for plans without has_location_map (viewset.py:119-121,1398-1399), so a Plan basico owner cannot disable the toggle at all. Plan basico is seeded with has_public_link=True, has_customization=True, has_location_map=False (SuscriptionApp seeds.py:45-73), so every published basico store leaks the owner's EncryptedCharField business domicilio to anonymous visitors. Correction to the hunter's framing: expired/lapsed subscriptions yield empty plan_benefits_of() so has_public_link fails and all public routes 404 — the affected population is stores on an ACTIVE plan lacking has_location_map (Plan basico). The leak additionally requires a StoreCustomization row (auto-created by get_or_create on the dashboard's GET /api/stores/customization/, viewset.py:1391) and a non-empty user.address.
root_cause: The has_location_map plan gate is enforced only in StorePublicSerializer.get_location_address; pattern_render.build_store_context and stores/services/contact.py contact_redirect_url independently derive the owner address / maps URL from raw UserProfile.address + customization.show_location without consulting profile_has_benefit('has_location_map'), and the /r/maps/ branch does not even honor the owner's show_location toggle.

title: Store MP webhook and public order-pay inherit the default anonymous throttles — shared Mercado Pago egress IPs may starve legitimate payment notifications
description: StoreMpWebhookView (POST /api/webhooks/store-mp/<slug>/) declares permission_classes=[AllowAny] and authentication_classes=[] but no throttle_classes, so DRF uses DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES = ResilientAnonRateThrottle + ResilientUserRateThrottle (settings.py:75-78). With no authentication, request.user is AnonymousUser: AnonRateThrottle keys throttle_anon_<ident> at 100/day and UserRateThrottle also applies to anonymous requests under throttle_user_<ident> at 1000/day (venv throttling.py:173-202). DaventProject.throttling pins REMOTE_ADDR into the ident (throttling.py:14-27,87-88), but neither default key has a per-view component, so every default-throttled anonymous endpoint shares the same cache key per cache backend/process. The platform MP webhook /api/payments/webhook/ is another AllowAny/default-throttled MP consumer (AdminApp/domains/payments/views/viewset_config.py:66-70), so store and subscription webhook traffic from the same provider egress IPs can share the anon bucket. If MP egress IPs are few and aggregate webhook volume from one IP exceeds the applicable anon cap, later legitimate signed notifications receive HTTP 429 in APIView.initial before HMAC verification, dedup, or StoreMpWebhookQuery run. PublicOrderPayView has the same default-throttle exposure for buyer IPs. Whether starvation occurs depends on MP egress IP distribution/volume, MP retry-on-429 behavior, the active deployment/cache topology, and cache health; none are fully source-visible.
claimed_root_cause: StoreMpWebhookView and PublicOrderPayView omit throttle_classes, so they inherit DRF DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES; for anonymous requests the anon scope enforces 100/day per pinned client IP in a cache key shared by every default-throttled endpoint (with a separate user scope adding a 1000/day IP-keyed bucket), and MP webhook egress IPs may be shared provider infrastructure — aggregate webhook volume from one egress IP can exceed the anon cap and 429 legitimate payment notifications before signature verification.

title: Support-chat image attachments bypass all storage quota AND all rate limiting — unbounded R2 growth per paid user
description: Every store-scoped image upload consumes the plan quota (Store.storage_used_bytes under select_for_update) or is a bounded staff/platform asset. Chat attachments are the sole exception: upload_chat_image validates (validate_image_file: ≤4MB, content-type allowlist, magic bytes), normalizes to WebP (imaging.normalize_image kind 'chat': ≤1600px, q78→floor 60), and PUTs to the DAVENT R2 bucket under key 'chat/<thread.id>/<uuid>.webp' — but never calls _check_quota/_consume_quota and ChatMessage stores only image_key, so no byte accounting exists anywhere. chat/ keys do not match _STORE_KEY_RE '^stores/(\d+)/' (storage.py:109) so they always land in the DAVENT bucket outside store.storage_used_bytes and outside BYO routing. Worse than the hunter claimed: the supposed 120/hour bound does not exist. ChatSendThrottle and ChatPollThrottle extend DRF ScopedRateThrottle, which reads the scope from view.throttle_scope (venv throttling.py:221) — and 'throttle_scope' appears nowhere in the repository, so self.scope becomes None and allow_request returns True unconditionally; the throttle classes' own scope attributes ('chat', 'chat_send') are shadowed and the settings rates (5000/h, 120/h) are never consulted. The view's throttle_classes=[ChatPollThrottle] also replaces DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES, so there is no fallback anon/user throttle either — /api/chat/send/ is effectively unthrottled. Remaining bounds: IsAuthenticated + chat_enabled gate (paid non-trial plan with has_support_chat, services.py:29-39), input normalization caps, and the annual purge_personal_data cron (default --days 365, only if scheduled — deployment fact). A user on the cheapest paid plan can therefore script unlimited ~350KB WebP objects into operator-owned R2, each also costing synchronous Pillow decode/encode CPU on gunicorn workers.
root_cause: upload_chat_image (AdminApp/domains/chat/services/attachments.py:27-45) performs validate_image_file + normalize_image + put_object with no quota check or accounting call; chat keys bypass _STORE_KEY_RE so they never touch store.storage_used_bytes; no per-user/per-thread attachment cap exists in send_message or the viewset; and the ScopedRateThrottle subclasses are dead code because no view defines throttle_scope.
intended_behavior: All client-driven object uploads should consume a bounded, plan- or user-scoped storage budget consistent with the quota model used by store images, proofs, feed media and AI-design images — or an equivalent explicit aggregate cap with prompt lifecycle cleanup — and the send endpoint should actually enforce the configured chat_send rate.

title: AnonRateThrottle subclasses skip authenticated users -> authenticated attacker gets unbounded password-reset emails (mail bombing / SMTP+queue abuse)
description: Every auth-endpoint throttle in AdminApp/domains/users/views/auth_views.py subclasses plain rest_framework AnonRateThrottle (LoginRateThrottle, RefreshRateThrottle, PasswordResetRateThrottle, PasswordResetConfirmRateThrottle, SocialAuthRateThrottle, PublicConfigRateThrottle). DRF's AnonRateThrottle.get_cache_key returns None when request.user.is_authenticated — and JWTAuthentication populates request.user on every request before check_throttles regardless of the view's AllowAny permission. Any registered user (open registration) therefore bypasses ALL these IP buckets entirely. The highest-impact instance is PasswordResetRequestView: each POST /api/password-reset/ for an existing email enqueues send_password_reset_email → a real SMTP send per request, with no per-user or per-email cap — unlimited mail-bombing of arbitrary victims through DAVENT's sender identity plus Celery/SMTP queue flooding that can delay transactional mail (invoices, verifications). The buyer-side code explicitly avoids AnonRateThrottle for exactly this reason ('NO se usa AnonRateThrottle porque saltaria la cuota a un comprador autenticado', customers auth_views.py:164-168) using a customer.pk-or-IP keyed throttle instead.
root_cause: Throttle classes chosen as AnonRateThrottle subclasses inherit the authenticated-skip semantics; no fallback per-user throttle exists on the AllowAny auth endpoints.
intended_behavior: Auth endpoints that emit side effects (emails, provider calls, token issuance) must be rate-limited for BOTH anonymous and authenticated principals — e.g., a SimpleRateThrottle keyed by user.pk when authenticated else IP, as the customer domain does.

title: Email-verification token is not bound to the email address: a stale link verifies a newly changed, never-proven email
description: EmailVerificationTokenGenerator._make_hash_value signs only user.pk + user.password + timestamp + profile.email_verified — user.email is absent. An authenticated user can PATCH /api/user/me/ to change user.email; UpdateUserQuery resets email_verified only when it was previously True, so a token issued while verified=False keeps identical hash inputs after the change. VerifyEmailQuery then sets email_verified=True for the new, never-proven address. StoreViewSet.create (viewset.py:463-469) treats that flag as the mailbox-control attestation for claiming a public store, while phone remains a separate requirement.
root_cause: _make_hash_value (services/services.py:202-209) omits user.email from the signed material, so the token proves only 'this user requested verification at time T', not 'this specific address was proven'.
intended_behavior: email_verified must attest control of the CURRENT user.email; changing the address must invalidate outstanding verification tokens (include the email — or a hash of it — in the token value).

GET /api/verify-email/?uid=&token= is AllowAny and calls VerifyEmailQuery.
after check_token succeeds, profile.email_verified=True is persisted for the account's current user.email.

impact.reason: Forges the email_verified attestation for an unproven address — defeats the store-claim anti-abuse email gate (phone anchor still required) and points account mail at an address the owner never authorized; no direct data exposure or account takeover.

title: Google social login auto-links by email without anti-pre-hijacking: pre-registered account stays accessible to attacker after victim's Google login
description: SocialLoginQuery resolves the account purely by email__iexact and, for an existing user, issues a session and sets email_verified=True — but never invalidates the password the account already had. Registration does not require email verification, so an attacker can pre-register a victim's email with their own password (and their own unique phone). When the real mailbox owner later uses 'Login with Google', Google proves email ownership and the backend logs them into the ATTACKER-CREATED account — while the attacker's password remains fully usable. Both parties hold persistent sessions for the same account: the attacker retains silent read/write access to everything the victim does (profile PII, store claim now unblocked because email_verified is set True, billing data). The sibling buyer-side implementation (google_customer_login) documents and fixes exactly this threat as 'Anti-pre-hijacking' by calling set_unusable_password() and sealing tokens_valid_after; the platform-users domain never received the port.
root_cause: SocialLoginQuery (services/social.py:103-147) performs find-or-create by verified provider email but, on the existing-account branch, only fills email_verified/names — it does not check whether the matched account's email was ever verified, does not invalidate a usable password, and does not revoke outstanding sessions. The credential proof covers the EMAIL, not the party who chose the existing password.
intended_behavior: Mirror the customer-side contract (StoreApp/domains/customers/services/google.py:153-165): when Google proves ownership of an email that matches a pre-existing account, any usable password must be invalidated and prior sessions sealed, so only the mailbox owner (via Google or password-reset) retains access.

RefreshToken.for_user(user) mints refresh+access for the Google-verified caller while the pre-registrant's password still authenticates via POST /api/token/

Sibling anti-pre-hijacking block: 'Google probó la titularidad del EMAIL, no quién eligió la contraseña' → set_unusable_password() + tokens_valid_after seal (lines 160-165)

title: Google login issues fresh sessions for is_active=False (deactivated) platform users
description: The platform password path is gated by Django's authenticate() -> ModelBackend.user_can_authenticate, which rejects is_active=False. The Google path bypasses that entirely: SocialLoginQuery looks the user up by email and _social_session_response calls RefreshToken.for_user(user) with no is_active check anywhere — for_user only logs a warning for inactive users (venv tokens.py:222-225) and still mints the tokens. However, the minted session is unusable: rest_framework_simplejwt's JWTAuthentication.get_user raises AuthenticationFailed for inactive users because CHECK_USER_IS_ACTIVE defaults True (simplejwt settings.py:47) and DaventProject SIMPLE_JWT does not override it — so every authenticated API call with the issued access token fails. Independently, the refresh endpoint itself rejects the token: TokenRefreshSerializer.validate applies USER_AUTHENTICATION_RULE → default_user_authentication_rule returns False for inactive users → 'no_active_account'. The deactivated principal obtains a 200 login response plus cookies but zero usable API access.
claimed_root_cause: Missing is_active gate on the federated session-issuance path: neither SocialLoginQuery (services/social.py:85-164) nor _social_session_response (views/auth_views.py:435-460) inspects user.is_active, unlike the password path which inherits the check from django.contrib.auth.authenticate.
